title: Tensed Metaphysics and Non-Local Grounding of Truth
kind: primary journal article; institutional repository PDF
locator: Selected full-text passages: supervaluationism/abstract-state discussion at printed p. 417 (PDF p. 7); challenge that future tense may not identify a unique grounding circumstance at pp. 418–420, especially pp. 418–419. Introductory framing and abstract also checked. Institutional repository copy, not publisher-hosted.
assumptions: Wawer's challenge targets C&R's proposal for grounding future-contingent truths; the counterfactual analogy concerns multiple relevant possibilities, and the supervaluationist option uses abstract possible states as continuations. This review does not assume his challenge succeeds.
conclusion: Wawer argues that a growing-block theorist can combine the ontology with supervaluationism over possible continuations, and asks how future tense selects the relevant grounding circumstances. Reviewer assessment: the passage suggests abstract states but does not itself provide a full semantics for concrete times and their ordering.
proof_status: Philosophical argument; selected passages read, no formal proof audit and no whole-article reconstruction claimed.
dependencies: Correia and Rosenkranz, Nothing to Come (2018), as discussed by Wawer; not independently read for this record.
open_questions: What exact semantics and modal base would make a growing-block supervaluationist account complete?
What principle, if any, selects a unique future grounding source without assuming the bivalence policy at issue?
relevance: Direct source for the grounding-source challenge and the restricted L/S counterinterpretation audit.
limits: Selected passages only; does not establish that Wawer's objection defeats C&R's account or provide a complete GBT semantics.

title: Replies to Critics
kind: primary journal article; full text accessed via ResearchGate
locator: Selected full-text sections: §6, pp. 471–477, on Wawer's grounding challenge and the conditional status of the grounding explanation; §7, pp. 477–482, on conditional later grounding and existential indeterminism. The article was not read cover to cover.
assumptions: C&R's later-grounding schema presupposes that the future-contingent sentence is presently true; their reply distinguishes the grounding requirement from the dispute over bivalence. Their §7 existential-indeterminism proposal uses world-states constituted by what exists simpliciter at a time. This record does not assume that these states map to the selected Einstein–scalar MGHD category.
conclusion: C&R defend later grounding as a conditional explanation that need not persuade someone who rejects its explanandum. They distinguish location-based from existence-based determinism/indeterminism, say GBT may admit existential indeterminism, and decline to claim that this vindicates the asymmetry intuition absent an argument for GBT.
proof_status: Philosophical reply; selected sections read, no formal proof audit or evaluation of all replies claimed.
dependencies: Jacek Wawer, ‘Tensed Metaphysics and Non-Local Grounding of Truth’ (2021), discussed in §6; read separately in selected passages for this review.
Stephan Torre's commentary on C&R, discussed in §7; not independently read for this record.
open_questions: How do C&R's nomological (DET_loc)/(DET_ex) alternatives and existence-worldstates map to maximal and nonmaximal developments in a specified relativistic matter theory?
What independent argument supports the relevant existence-worldstate category and its modal alternatives?
relevance: Primary source for the fair treatment of conditional later grounding and the exact scope of C&R's existential-openness proposal.
limits: Only §§6–7 were read directly. The chapter 7 original-clause summary is separately available in research/future-truth-rival-chapters/CLAUSES.md; it records (DET_loc)/(DET_ex) as explicitly nomological, but that extraction is not this source record or a full-book read.
